transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Saturday, September 19. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Trump signs Russia sanctions bill into law, allowing up to 100 percent tariffs on India. President Trump has officially enacted a new sanctions law aimed at Russia and Iran, empowering the U.S. to impose penalties on nations purchasing Russian energy supplies. Countries like India and China, significant buyers of Russian crude and gas, have raised concerns about the potential impact on India US reaches deal with Denmark for 'permanent security control' over Greenland. The United States and Denmark are in the final stages of discussions to enhance US military operations in Greenland. This strategic arrangement will not infringe on Greenland's autonomy, affirming its status as a Danish territory. The talks also involve strategies to curb Chinese activity in this vital Arctic locale. A potential agreement might include establishing a US missile defense system, with an official update expected shortly. Pawan Sehrawat replaces Tajinderpal Singh Toor as India's Asian Games flag-bearer. Pawan Sehrawat has been chosen as the flag-bearer for India's opening ceremony at the Asian Games, stepping in for Tajinderpal Singh Toor, who faced delays with his official kit. Toor mentioned that his kit would arrive too late to participate in the event. Additionally, the athletics team is still waiting for their uniforms. Sehrawat will accompany Manu Bhaker in carrying the Indian flag. Meet Dina McCormick, whom Zuckerberg asked to trade her Meta board seat for a job. Born in Cairo, Egypt and raised in Texas, Dina Powell McCormick gave up her Meta board seat last December after Mark Zuckerberg asked her to take an operating job instead. Nine months on, the Goldman Sachs veteran and former deputy national security adviser is president, vice chairman and co-leader of Meta Compute, handling the company's hardest legal, political and financial problems as its 2026 AI capex guidance climbs to as much as $145 billion. Trump bans news outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House. President Donald Trump has enacted a swift exclusion of three major news outlets, CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, from White House premises. He branded their regular reports as 'FAKE NEWS,' marking a bold stance against media he perceives as adversarial. Trump warned that more outlets could follow if they continue to publish misleading narratives about his presidency. Extremely speedy action by probe agency can create doubt: SC. The speed at which CBI sprang into action on a bribery complaint and laid a trap within hours to catch a public servant could give rise to suspicion, which, Supreme Court said, could not be brushed aside and had to be examined. $1.75m historic home mirrors Swift and Kelce's $5.35m Ohio mansion. A historic mansion linked to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio estate has hit the market for $1.75 million. The House of Seven Gables in Illinois spans 10,000 square feet with seven bedrooms and was designed by the same architect who created Kelce's 21,000-square-foot Moyenage estate overlooking Lake Erie. Rod Stewart's former LA estate flips from $6.25m to $86m after restoration. A legendary estate in Holmby Hills, previously owned by Rod Stewart, has fetched an impressive $86 million. The sprawling six-acre property was split into two parcels, with television producer David Zander acquiring the main mansion for $57 million. Meanwhile, Nick Kaiser purchased a smaller parcel complete with a historic cabin for $29 million. This notable sale underscores the ongoing allure of grand historic properties. MHA cites internal security issues to defend FCRA tweak. Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especially Christians, Union home ministry asserted Friday that the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space", which Centre is fully entitled to protect, and emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation. Google cofounder Larry Page's wife's company has donated over $120m in ocean projects. Lucinda Southworth, married to Google co-founder Larry Page, is a passionate advocate for ocean conservation through her organization, Oceankind. Since 2018, Oceankind has generously contributed over $120 million to improve marine ecosystems and support community health. With a focus on addressing pressing challenges like climate change and pollution, the organization champions innovative solutions and effective policies to protect our oceans worldwide. Asian Games: Trouble in Japan! Indian athletes face housing, food and transport chaos. Torrential rains battered this city last week, forcing evacuations, disrupting train services and even prompting the rescheduling of some Asian Games events.
